thread:
alex: Quick postmortem follow-up from last night
we hit a sustained GPU surge in eu-west-1, autoscaler lagged ~6m because quota bump didn't arrive in time, scheduler kept packing pods onto a few nodes causing headroom starvation and model fallbacks. I summarized the immediate fixes in the doc: https://redwood.internal/postmortems/2025-03-gpu-surge. Can we capture owners + timelines for remediation?

maria: reading. thanks for the summary. i can take scheduler tuning (priority/slice changes + backoff). i'll start with a conservative change and can test in staging tomorrow. :thumbsup:

kevin: i'll own quota ops — open a ticket with the cloud team for soft quota increases and a process to pre-warm quota when we flip heavy traffic windows. will add request by EOD.

priya: i'll handle headroom planning simulations and a runbook entry for surge-mode pre-warm. propose a 10% baseline extra headroom for peak windows and a checklist to trigger 30m before expected spikes. i'll prototype simulation using last 3 months of traffic.

alex: thanks. let's make the deliverables explicit:
- maria: scheduler tunables PR (config + rollout plan) by 2025-03-28
- kevin: quota request + escalation path documented by 2025-03-26
- priya: headroom sim results + runbook draft by 2025-04-02
Can each of you post a one-line status update when you start? i'll track in the postmortem follow-up sheet.

maria: noted. starting tomorrow morning. initial change: increase scheduler preemption threshold and lower packFactor for gpuloaded pods. sample snippet i'll test in staging:
```yaml
autoscaler:
  target_utilization: 0.7
  packFactor: 0.6  # reduce aggressive bin-packing
  preemption_threshold: 0.85
```
won't ship to prod without canary.

kevin: ticket created: CLOUD-1429. cc @platform-ops. included expected spike windows and request for burst quota of +15 GPUs for two hours during peaks. ETA cloud ack: 48-72h. documenting escalation (oncall -> cloud-sales -> account mgr).

priya: kicked off sim run (script uses historical seq len distro + request rate). quick note: prefix caching made peak cost look lower than raw token rate, so headroom needs to account for worst-case cache miss patterns. will upload results to the follow-up sheet by Monday.

alex: good. also two housekeeping items: 1) add an automated blackout detector so we can trigger standby capacity earlier, 2) postmortem follow-up check on 2025-04-06 to review action closure.

maria: re: blackout detector — opened infra issue INFRA-678. simple rule: if >80% of GPUs in zone saturated for 3m trigger standby scale-up and page ops. will prototype as a cron job + alert.

sre-bot: Reminder: follow-up meeting scheduled by alex for 2025-04-06 16:00 UTC (channel: #incidents, agenda pinned).

kevin: cloud responded: can pre-approve burst quota for monthly peaks if we provide a sustained usage graph + contact list. i'll compile and ask priya for the sim export to attach. :spiral_calendar:

priya: uploaded sim csv and run notes to the follow-up sheet. early results: a 12% extra GPU headroom reduces fallback events by ~90% for the tested window. will refine and include 95th/99th percentile scenarios.

alex: perfect. next steps for closure: owners to update the sheet with PR links/ticket numbers, we'll mark items as in-progress. i'll do the 04-06 check and close out items or extend timelines as needed. thanks all. :heart:

deploy-bot: Canary scheduled for scheduler tunables change in staging at 2025-03-27T02:00:00Z. Monitor metrics: gpu_utilization, pod_evictions, autoscaler_latency.

maria: noted, watching the canary. will post results in thread after run.

kevin: cloud approved soft burst for next two monthly windows pending usage docs. filing follow-up with finance for cost sign-off.

alex: closing loop — marking thread as action-tracked. we'll keep communications short here and update the follow-up sheet. Thanks everyone.
